Neural Representations of Multilayer Social Network Information Analysis: Univariate Analyses

Ovidia Stanoi

4/12/2025

In this script, we ran 3 regression models. The first model (Model 1) estimates participants’ neural responses to peers’ faces in our 9 ROIs as a function of how much more status peers have relative to them in a dual space that includes information from both the popularity and leadership dimension (dual_relative_status). The second model (Model 2) estimates participants’ neural responses to peers’ faces in the 9 ROIs as a function of how much more popularity status peers have relative to them. In practice, we estimated participants’ mean neural response to each peer face as a function of that peer’s popularity status, while holding constant the perceiver’s own popularity status. By including the participants’ own status in the model, the parameter of the relationship between the target’s status and neural activity provides an estimate of participants’ mean response to the targets’ status relative to their own. The third model (Model 3) estimates participants’ neural responses to peers’ faces in the 9 ROIs as a function of how much more leadership status peers have relative to them. The same method was used as in Model 2. To account for multiple comparisons, all models are run in a multilevel framework with random slopes per ROI. We also included random intercepts for perceivers and targets, nested within groups. No control variables were included in these models.

Clear global environment.

remove(list=ls())

Open packages.

library("tidyverse")
library("corrplot")
library("reshape")
library("rstanarm")
library("bmlm")
library("flextable")
library("officer")
library("performance")

Set up ggplot theme.

theme_set(theme_bw() +
            theme(plot.title = element_text(size=14, hjust = .5),
                  axis.text=element_text(size=12),
                  axis.title=element_text(size=13),
                  # plot.title = element_text(size=20, hjust = .5), # use this for .pdf version of figures instead of .html
                  # axis.text=element_text(size=20),  # use this for .pdf version of figures instead of .html
                  # axis.title=element_text(size=22), # use this for .pdf version of figures instead of .html
                  axis.line = element_line(colour = "gray"),
                  panel.border = element_rect(colour = "gray"),
                  panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
                  axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 15, hjust = 1),
                  panel.background = element_rect(colour = "gray", linewidth = .8),
                  legend.position = "none"))

Set up the file directory.

path <- ""

Read the dataset including each participant’s ROI-level neural responses to different faces and status information.

d <- read.csv(sprintf("%s/Data/univariate_dataset.csv", path)) %>%
  select(groupID, pid, face, roi, neural_response, dual_relative_status_cw,
         face_like_strength_in_cw, face_leader_strength_in_cw, 
         pid_like_strength_in_cw, pid_leader_strength_in_cw)

Check the format of the dataset.

head(d)

1 Model 1 (Relative Dual Status)

Run regression model for relative dual status.

# options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())
# m <- stan_glmer(neural_response ~ dual_relative_status_cw +
#                   (1 | groupID:pid) + (1 | groupID:face) +
#                   (dual_relative_status_cw | roi),
#             data = d,  iter = 4000,
#             control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99),
#             seed = 123)
# save(m, file = sprintf("%s/Model Results/Univariate_Model_2D_Relative_Status_no_controls.RData", path))

Obtain ROI-level varying betas for the main effect of targets’ relative dual status measures on the perceivers’ ROI-level neural responses.

# 0. Load model results
load(sprintf("%s/Model Results/Univariate_Model_2D_Relative_Status_no_controls.RData", path))

# 1.a. draws for overall mean
mu_b_sims <- as.matrix(m, 
                       pars = "dual_relative_status_cw")
# 1.b. draws for roi-level error
b_sims <- as.matrix(m, 
                    regex_pars = "b\\[dual_relative_status_cw roi:")

# 1.c. draws for roi-level varying slopes               
b_sims <- as.numeric(mu_b_sims) + b_sims          

# 2. Compute mean, SD, and 95% credible interval of varying slopes
# 2.a. Posterior mean and SD of each beta
b_mean <- apply(X = b_sims,     # posterior mean
                MARGIN = 2,
                FUN = mean)
b_sd <- apply(X = b_sims,       # posterior SD
              MARGIN = 2,
              FUN = sd)
# 2.b. Posterior 95% credible interval
b_quant <- apply(X = b_sims, 
                 MARGIN = 2, 
                 FUN = quantile, 
                 probs = c(0.025, 0.975))

# 2.c. Create a CI data frame
b_quant <- data.frame(t(b_quant))
names(b_quant) <- c("beta_Q2.5", "beta_Q97.5")

# 3. Combine summary statistics of posterior simulation draws
b_df <- data.frame(b_mean, b_sd, b_quant)

# 4. Clean dataset
b_df$roi <- sub(".*:", "", rownames(b_df))
b_df$roi <- sub("]", "", b_df$roi)
b_df$beta_2d <- b_df$b_mean
b_df$sd <- b_df$b_sd
b_df$low_ci <- b_df$beta_Q2.5 
b_df$upp_ci <- b_df$beta_Q97.5
rownames(b_df) <- NULL

# 5. Select only the columns we need: roi, beta, sd, low_ci, upp_ci
b_df <- subset(b_df, select = c(roi, beta_2d, sd, low_ci, upp_ci))

# 6. Rename ROIs and separate in 3 categories: valuation, soc cog, relational binding
b_df <- b_df %>%
  mutate(roi = dplyr::recode(roi, 
                             "Saxe_dmPFC" = "dmPFC",
                             "HO_amygdala" = "Amygdala",
                             "r_HPC" = "rHPC",       
                             "r_TPJ" = "rTPJ",       
                             "Kable_VS" = "VS",
                             "ERC" = "ERC",
                             "l_HPC" = "lHPC",
                             "l_TPJ" = "lTPJ"),
         roi = factor(roi, levels = c("vmPFC", "Amygdala", "VS", 
                                          "dmPFC", "rTPJ", "lTPJ",
                                          "rHPC", "lHPC", "ERC")),
         roi_type = ifelse(roi %in% c("vmPFC", "Amygdala", "VS"), "valuation",
                        ifelse(roi %in% c("dmPFC", "rTPJ", "lTPJ"), "social_cognition",
                               "relational_binding")))

# 7. Plot betas' posterior mean and 95% credible interval
ggplot(data = b_df, 
       aes(x = roi, 
           y = beta_2d)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, 
             linewidth = 0.9, linetype = 2) + 
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = low_ci, 
                      ymax = upp_ci, color = roi_type), 
                   size = 1.2, linewidth = .9) + 
                   # size = 2, linewidth = 2.5) + 
  scale_color_manual(values = c("goldenrod2", "dodgerblue4", "darkgreen")) +
  labs(x = "ROI", y = "Effect of a Target's Dual Relative Status 
  on the Perceiver's Neural Response") 

# ggsave(sprintf("%s/Figures/univariate_multilevel_roi_beta_results_2D_relative_status_no_controls.pdf", path),
#          units="in", width=15, height=7, dpi=300)

# 8. Save beta results 
write.csv(b_df, (sprintf("%s/Data/univariate_multilevel_roi_beta_results_2D_relative_status_no_controls.csv", path)),
          row.names = F)

Check results.

# Arrange data
b_df_table <- b_df %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 2)),
         CI_95 = paste0("[", round(low_ci, 2), ", ", round(upp_ci, 2), "]")) %>%
  select(-c(low_ci, upp_ci, roi_type)) %>%
  arrange(roi)

# Create table of results  
b_df_table <- flextable(b_df_table) %>%
  set_header_labels(roi = "ROI",
    beta_2d = "Beta Estimate",
    sd = "SE",
    CI_95 = "95% CI") %>%
  autofit() %>%
  theme_booktabs()

# Save to Word document
doc <- read_docx() %>%
  body_add_par("Table: Univariate Results: Effect of Target's Relative Dual Status on ROI Neural Activity", 
               style = "heading 2") %>%
  body_add_flextable(b_df_table)

print(doc, target = sprintf("%s/Tables/univariate_multilevel_roi_beta_results_2D_relative_status_no_controls.docx", path))

b_sims <- data.frame(b_sims)

# vmPFC

Create a scatterplot that shows the relationship between targets’ relative dual status and perceivers’ neural responses in the vmPFC.

# Extract posterior distributions - 
# main and random effects for intercept & vmPFC 
b_sims <- as.data.frame(m, 
                       pars = c("(Intercept)", "b[(Intercept) roi:vmPFC]",
                                "dual_relative_status_cw", 
                                "b[dual_relative_status_cw roi:vmPFC]"))

# Calculate the vmPFC-specific effects  
b_sims$intercept <- b_sims$`(Intercept)` + b_sims$`b[(Intercept) roi:vmPFC]`
b_sims$b_dual_relative_status <- b_sims$dual_relative_status_cw + b_sims$`b[dual_relative_status_cw roi:vmPFC]`

# Extract all posterior distributions
p <- b_sims %>%
  select(intercept, b_dual_relative_status)

p <- p %>%
  dplyr::mutate(draw = 1:8000,
         m_int = median(intercept), # Extract fixed effects medians from the model
         m_b_dual_relative_status = median(b_dual_relative_status))  # Extract fixed effects median from the model

# Sample random draws
nr_random_draws <- 8000 # specify here number of random draws

# Create a dataframe that includes predicted y values for each random draw
p2 <- p[rep(seq_len(nrow(p)), each = 6), ] %>%
  mutate(seq = rep(-1:4, nr_random_draws)) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(y_draw = intercept + b_dual_relative_status * seq,
         y_fe = m_int + m_b_dual_relative_status * seq)

# Plot results 
ggplot() +
  labs(y = "Perceiver's vmPFC Neural Response", 
       x = "Target's Dual Relative Status") +
  geom_line(data = p2, aes(x = seq, y = y_draw, group = draw), 
            color = "darkgreen", alpha = .1, size = .1) +
  geom_line(data = p2, aes(x = seq, y = y_fe), color = "black", size = 2) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0))  

# ggsave(file = sprintf("%s/Figures/univariate_vmpfc_2D_scatterplot_no_controls.pdf", path),
#        units="in", width=7, height=6, dpi=300)

Run regression model for relative popularity status alone.

Obtain ROI-level varying betas for the main effect of a target’s popularity status measure on the perceiver’s ROI-level neural responses. Since we are controlling in the model for the perceiver’s popularity status, this is in effect a measure of the target’s relative popularity status.

# 0. Load model results
load(sprintf("%s/Model Results/Univariate_Model_Popularity_Relative_Status_no_controls.RData", path))

# 1.a. draws for overall mean
mu_b_sims <- as.matrix(m2, 
                       pars = "face_like_strength_in_cw")
# 1.b. draws for roi-level error
b_sims <- as.matrix(m2, 
                    regex_pars = "b\\[face_like_strength_in_cw roi:")

# 1.c. draws for roi-level varying slopes               
b_sims <- as.numeric(mu_b_sims) + b_sims          

# 2. Compute mean, SD, and 95% credible interval of varying slopes
# 2.a. Posterior mean and SD of each beta
b_mean <- apply(X = b_sims,     # posterior mean
                MARGIN = 2,
                FUN = mean)
b_sd <- apply(X = b_sims,       # posterior SD
              MARGIN = 2,
              FUN = sd)

# 2.b. Posterior 95% credible interval
b_quant <- apply(X = b_sims, 
                 MARGIN = 2, 
                 FUN = quantile, 
                 probs = c(0.025, 0.975))

# 2.c. Create a CI data frame
b_quant <- data.frame(t(b_quant))
names(b_quant) <- c("beta_Q2.5", "beta_Q97.5")

# 3. Combine summary statistics of posterior simulation draws
b_df <- data.frame(b_mean, b_sd, b_quant)

# 4. Clean dataset
b_df$roi <- sub(".*:", "", rownames(b_df))
b_df$roi <- sub("]", "", b_df$roi)
b_df$beta_like <- b_df$b_mean
b_df$sd <- b_df$b_sd
b_df$low_ci <- b_df$beta_Q2.5 
b_df$upp_ci <- b_df$beta_Q97.5
rownames(b_df) <- NULL

# 5. Select only the columns we need: roi, beta, sd, low_ci, upp_ci
b_df <- subset(b_df, select = c(roi, beta_like, sd, low_ci, upp_ci))

# 6. Rename ROIs and separate in 3 categories: valuation, soc cog, relational binding
b_df <- b_df %>%
  mutate(roi = dplyr::recode(roi, 
                             "Saxe_dmPFC" = "dmPFC",
                             "HO_amygdala" = "Amygdala",
                             "r_HPC" = "rHPC",       
                             "r_TPJ" = "rTPJ",       
                             "Kable_VS" = "VS",
                             "ERC" = "ERC",
                             "l_HPC" = "lHPC",
                             "l_TPJ" = "lTPJ"),
         roi = factor(roi, levels = c("vmPFC", "Amygdala", "VS", 
                                          "dmPFC", "rTPJ", "lTPJ",
                                          "rHPC", "lHPC", "ERC")),
         roi_type = ifelse(roi %in% c("vmPFC", "Amygdala", "VS"), "valuation",
                        ifelse(roi %in% c("dmPFC", "rTPJ", "lTPJ"), "social_cognition",
                               "relational_binding")))

# 7. Plot betas' posterior means and 95% credible intervals
ggplot(data = b_df, 
       aes(x = roi, 
           y = beta_like)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, 
             linewidth = 0.9, linetype = 2) + 
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = low_ci, 
                      ymax = upp_ci, color = roi_type), 
                  size = 1.2, linewidth = .9) + 
  scale_color_manual(values = c("goldenrod2", "dodgerblue4", "darkgreen")) +
  labs(x = "ROI", y = "ROI-Level Betas & 95% CIs",
       title = "Effect of Target's Relative Popularity Status on ROI Neural Activity")

write.csv(b_df, (sprintf("%s/Data/univariate_multilevel_roi_beta_results_popularity_relative_status_no_controls.csv", path)),

# 2. Compute mean, SD, and 95% credible interval of varying slopes

# 3. Combine summary statistics of posterior simulation draws

# 4. Clean dataset
b_df$roi <- sub(".*:", "", rownames(b_df))
b_df$roi <- sub("]", "", b_df$roi)

                        ifelse(roi %in% c("dmPFC", "rTPJ", "lTPJ"), "social_cognition",
                               "relational_binding")))

# 7. Plot betas' posterior means and 95% credible intervals
ggplot(data = b_df, 
       aes(x = roi, 
           y = beta_leader)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, 
             linewidth = 0.9, linetype = 2) + 
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = low_ci, 
                      ymax = upp_ci, color = roi_type), 
                  size = 1.2, linewidth = .9) + 
  scale_color_manual(values = c("goldenrod2", "dodgerblue4", "darkgreen")) +
  labs(x = "ROI", y = "ROI-Level Betas & 95% CIs",
       title = "Effect of Target's Relative Leadership Status on ROI Neural Activity") 

# ggsave(sprintf("%s/Figures/univariate_multilevel_roi_beta_results_leadership_relative_status_no_controls.pdf", path),
#        units="in", width=12, height=7, dpi=300)

# 8. Save beta results 
write.csv(b_df, (sprintf("%s/Data/univariate_multilevel_roi_beta_results_leadership_relative_status_no_controls.csv", path)),
          row.names = F)

Check results.

# Arrange data
b_df_table <- b_df %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 2)),
         CI_95 = paste0("[", round(low_ci, 2), ", ", round(upp_ci, 2), "]")) %>%
  select(-c(low_ci, upp_ci, roi_type)) %>%
  arrange(roi)

# Create table of results  
b_df_table <- flextable(b_df_table) %>%
  set_header_labels(roi = "ROI",
    beta_leader = "Beta Estimate",
    sd = "SE",
    CI_95 = "95% CI") %>%
  autofit() %>%
  theme_booktabs()
